title: Linked Lists
subtitle: Treat a list as a graph of node identities: preserve reachability while you rewire one boundary at a time.
variables: n,m = reachable node counts; k = group size or number of lists; h = heap size <= k; N = total nodes across lists. Unless stated otherwise lists are finite, acyclic, singly linked, values compare in O(1), and nodes use identity equality/hash. Auxiliary space excludes existing nodes and returned newly allocated nodes; recursion frames count. Pointer access/rewiring is O(1), locating a node is O(n). Python arbitrary-size arithmetic and comparison can add bit-length costs; hash bounds are expected. Mutation may affect every alias to a node; no concurrent mutation.
